passage:
A geography lesson described families who had to move because their farms became too dry to support them. Students discussed climate migration.
One student said moving sounded simple. Another pointed out that leaving home means losing neighbors, schools, jobs, and familiar graves.
The teacher asked students to write from the view of a teenager moving to a new city because of environmental change.
The writing made the topic more human.
Climate change is often shown with numbers and graphs. Those are important, but behind every number may be a family packing bags. Migration is not only movement. It is loss and beginning together.
